    <bpmn:task id="Task_InformEmployee" name="Inform employee that meal is in service hatch"/>

    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_CallGuest" name="Call for guest" messageRef="Msg_Call"/>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_HandMeal" name="Hand over meal at service hatch" messageRef="Msg_MealHandover"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="FR_7" sourceRef="Task_InformChef" targetRef="ManualTask_PrepareMeal"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="FR_8" sourceRef="ManualTask_PrepareMeal" targetRef="ManualTask_PlaceInHatch"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="FR_9" sourceRef="ManualTask_PlaceInHatch" targetRef="Task_InformEmployee"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="FR_10" sourceRef="Task_InformEmployee" targetRef="SendTask_SetOffBuzzer"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="FR_12" sourceRef="Gateway_EmpWait" targetRef="IntermediateCatch_GuestAtHatch"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="FR_13" sourceRef="Gateway_EmpWait" targetRef="Timer_5Minutes"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="FR_17" sourceRef="SendTask_HandMeal" targetRef="EndEvent_Restaurant"/>
  </bpmn:process>

rules.instruction: When the description says the flow of a participant continues only after a stated occurrence happens, such as another party informing it that an item is ready, and the description names no alternative trigger for that continuation: Model that occurrence as one intermediate catch event on the waiting participant's flow, placed directly before the step it enables. Do not model the waiting itself as a task, and do not add an event-based gateway with an additional alternative catch event unless the description names several alternative triggers.
rules.situation: the description says the flow of a participant continues only after a stated occurrence happens, such as another party informing it that an item is ready, and the description names no alternative trigger for that continuation

rules.instruction: When the description states one sentence in which a performer or performer group carries out two distinct activities joined by 'and', where the second activity responds to or resolves issues raised by the first: Model each of the two activities as its own task, in the order stated in the sentence, connected by a sequence flow. Do not merge them into one task whose label combines both actions, and do not drop either activity from the model.
rules.situation: the description joins two or more distinct actions performed by the same actor in one sentence or one consecutive sequence (for example, an action on a system followed by an action on a person or an item, or preparing an item and then handing it to another party)

rules.instruction: When the description has one role that performs its own sequence of steps and tells another role that a piece of work is finished, and the informed role's next step can only proceed after that notice arrives: Model the notice as a message flow from the informing task in the informing role's pool to an intermediate message catch event in the informed role's pool. Place that catch event after the informed role's own preceding step and before its next step. Do not model the wait as an event-based gateway, a send task, or a sequence flow from the other role. Do not add a separate event for a different message that the description does not mention.
rules.situation: the description has one role that performs its own sequence of steps and tells another role that a piece of work is finished, and the informed role's next step can only proceed after that notice arrives

rules.instruction: When the description says that a participant is handed a device or notice that will later announce readiness, and that the participant then waits for that announcement before continuing to collect the result: When this holds, model the participant's wait as an intermediate catch event that is triggered by the later announcement, placed on the participant's path before the collection step. Model the announcing action on the other side as an intermediate throw event or a send task. Do not model the wait as a task, and do not connect the collection step directly without the catch event.
rules.situation: the description says that a participant is handed a device or notice that will later announce readiness, and that the participant then waits for that announcement before continuing to collect the result

rules.instruction: When the description lists several consecutive actions by the same participant, each stated in its own sentence or clause and each acting on a different resource or counterpart (for example, recording an entry in a system, then collecting something from a counterpart, then setting up an item and handing it over, then informing another party), before the flow moves on: Model each such action as its own task in that participant's lane, in the order the description states them, connected by sequence flows. Do not drop any stated action, and do not fold it into a neighbouring task. Keep each action as a separate task even when the next action follows directly with no stated pause.
rules.situation: the description lists several consecutive actions by the same participant, each stated in its own sentence or clause and each acting on a different resource or counterpart (for example, recording an entry in a system, then collecting something from a counterpart, then setting up an item and handing it over, then informing another party), before the flow moves on

rules.instruction: When the description says one participant passes an order, a request, or the news of a finished item on to another participant, and the receiving participant's flow either begins with that passing-on or continues only after it: Model the sending side as a plain task in the sender's pool, not as a sendTask. Model the receiving side in the receiver's pool as a message start event if the passed-on item begins the receiver's process, or as an intermediate message catch event placed before the step it enables if the receiver's flow continues only after it. Connect the two with one message flow from the sending task to that event. Do not model the receiving side as a receiveTask, and do not pair a sendTask with a receiveTask for the same exchange.
rules.situation: the description says one participant passes an order, a request, or the news of a finished item on to another participant, and the receiving participant's flow either begins with that passing-on or continues only after it

promoted.trigger: the description says that an actor is given an indicator that will later signal that something is ready, and that the actor must hold off on the next step until that signal arrives
promoted.instruction: When this holds, model the actor's pause as an intermediate catch event triggered by the later signal, placed on the actor's path before the next step. Model the signalling action on the other side as an intermediate throw event or a send task. Do not model the pause as a task, and do not connect the next step directly without the catch event.
promoted.detail: general form of EXS-051, written after it improved the model of example 24

promoted.trigger: the description lists several consecutive actions by the same participant, each stated in its own sentence or clause and each acting on a different resource or other party, before the flow moves on
promoted.instruction: Model each such action as its own task in that participant's lane, in the order stated, connected by sequence flows. Do not drop any stated action or merge it into a neighbouring task, even when the next action follows immediately without a stated pause.
promoted.detail: general form of EXS-052, written after it improved the model of example 24
